newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends off, bearish API data seen.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends off, bearish API data seen.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline prices eased Tuesday ahead of weekly oil inventory data which traders expected would show increasing gasoline supplies and give a bearish direction to a rangebound market.
"The market seems to be waiting with bated breath for the API numbers, and if they come in as expected, the market could go much lower," said Mike De Luca, trader with Prudential Securities.
June gasoline settled 0.23 cent lower at 60.31 cents a gallon.
June crude ended up three cents a barrel at $19.66 though significantly off its session high of $19.84. June heating oil finished 0.48 cent a gallon higher at 53.53 cents.
Oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) is expected by traders and analysts to show a one to two million barrel rise in gasoline stocks.
Dealers attributed the expected stock rise to higher refinery output and an anticipated decrease in implied demand for gasoline.
Gasoline implied demand in the past two weeks of data was above a lofty eight million barrels a day which dealers thought was unrealistic.
Tuesday's data reflects the week ended May 2.
Crude stocks are seen rising one to three million barrels, extending several consecutive weeks of builds driven by imports from across the Atlantic.
Dealers expect the data may lead to a downside break of the $19.50 to $20.50 a barrel range crude has been trading in since late April.

Meanwhile, traders expect a minor draw in distillate stocks as uneasonably cold weather in the U.S. has drained heating oil supply. The tighter supply has provided springtime strength to heating oil prices, and dealers expect the API data to report a drop in distillate stocks of as much as one million barrels.
Distillate stocks are comprised of heating oil and diesel.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
